newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Bancorex sacks top executives - televisions.
newsitem.headline: Romania Bancorex sacks top executives - televisions.

text.p: A shareholders' meeting of Romania's leading state-run Bancorex SA commercial bank has decided to sack chairman Razvan Temesan and his deputy, local television stations reported on Friday.
"Sources with Bancorex have declared that both the bank chairman (Razvan Temesan) and vice-chairman Alexandru Ghiba were sacked," the state television said. It did not elaborate.

The move followed a board meeting with its main shareholder -- the State Ownership Fund, said the private Pro TV station, which carried the same report. Neither Temesan nor other officials were available for comment.
Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA, specialised in foreign trade financing, handles the bulk of foreign exchange trading on the local market.

The latest data show the bank has share capital of 93.2 billion lei, with the State Ownership Fund holding 63 percent and private ownership funds some 27 percent. The rest goes to corporations and individuals. According to latest available data, its gross profit over January-June 1996 was 159.8 billion lei, with total assets of 8.3 trillion lei last June.
Last year, Banking rating service Thomson BankWatch awarded Bancorex a LC-1 short-term local currency debt rating, implying a very high likelihood of interest and principle for the bank.
This month, Moody's Investors Service assigned Bancorex's long-term deposits a B1 rating and a not-prime for the short-term ones.
